findings.action: The non-Unix implementation is a no-op. On supported Windows builds, a go-build directory containing a 200 MiB test binary still reaches the 128 MiB runtime inventory and prevents cleanup, preserving the defect R1 requires this scope to fix. Cross-build and vet checks establish compilation, not this behavior; the functional regression skips every non-Linux platform. Implement equivalent bounded cleanup on supported platforms, or explicitly amend the requirement and delivery claims to exclude them.

Readdirnames(-1) materializes every directory entry before consulting the 200,000-entry budget at lines 92-94. A leftover with arbitrarily many entries therefore consumes unbounded enumeration memory and time before overflow can return incomplete, defeating the bounded-inventory requirement and potentially exhausting the cleanup process. Read bounded batches and enforce the remaining budget during enumeration. The new top-level fs.ReadDir at review_adapter_containment.go:618 likewise enumerates all runtime entries before the ordinary inventory applies.

A directory moved outside the runtime after listing but before Openat can be replaced by a FIFO or symlink, or disappear. ENOTDIR, ELOOP and ENOENT then return success without confirming the original directory's removal. The ordinary runtime inventory removes the replacement and cleanup can report completion while the original remains elsewhere, contrary to R3. The synchronized test at review_go_build_cleanup_unix_test.go:52 constructs this window but discards the cleanup error at line 75. Preserve and verify the identity observed before opening, fail incomplete when it changes, and require that error in the regression while retaining nonblocking opens.

unix.Dup clears FD_CLOEXEC, and os.NewFile does not restore it. During directory enumeration, a concurrently executed child can inherit this directory descriptor, extending its lifetime and exposing another cleanup directory through descriptor-relative access. Local syscall probing confirmed that the duplicate lacks close-on-exec and survives exec; Go's exec implementation relies on close-on-exec for unrelated descriptors. Duplicate atomically with F_DUPFD_CLOEXEC or an equivalent operation; setting the flag afterward leaves a concurrent fork window.
